findings.text: You must create an app with your OAuth provider before connecting it to your Stripe App.
findings.quote: If you haven’t already, create an app with your OAuth provider to connect and use with your Stripe App.

findings.text: Stripe Apps require the OAuth provider to support PKCE.
findings.quote: Ensure that your OAuth provider supports the Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE) flow.

findings.text: The code challenge method must be S256.
findings.quote:
code_challenge_method

This is always S256.

findings.text: The response type for the authorization request is always code.
findings.quote:
response_type

This is always code. The PKCE flow uses code as the value to request an authorization code from the OAuth provider.

findings.text: The grant type for retrieving an access token is always authorization_code.
findings.quote:
grant_type

This is always authorization_code.

findings.text: Register the sandbox and live redirect URLs with your OAuth provider.
findings.quote: Register both URLs with your OAuth provider.

findings.text: Add the secret_write permission to your app to store secrets.
findings.quote:
Add the secret_write permission to your app:

Command Line

stripe apps grant permission "secret_write" "Allows storing secrets between page reloads"

findings.text: The authorization code expires in 5 minutes.
findings.quote: An authorization code you can use in the next call to get an access token for your user. This can only be used once and expires in 5 minutes.

findings.text: The only supported response type is code.
findings.quote: The only option at the moment is code.

findings.text: The authorization endpoint is https://connect.stripe.com/oauth/authorize.
findings.quote: GET https://connect.stripe.com/oauth/authorize

findings.text: The token endpoint is https://connect.stripe.com/oauth/token.
findings.quote: POST https://connect.stripe.com/oauth/token

findings.text: Consuming an authorization code more than once revokes the account connection.
findings.quote: Per OAuth v2, this endpoint isn’t idempotent. Consuming an authorization code more than once revokes the account connection.

findings.text: Redirect URIs must exactly match one of the configured values and live mode must use HTTPS.
findings.quote: If provided, this must exactly match one of the comma-separated redirect_uri values in your application settings. To protect yourself from certain forms of man-in-the-middle attacks, the live mode redirect_uri must use a secure HTTPS connection.

findings.text: The supported grant types are authorization_code and refresh_token.
findings.quote: Unsupported grant_type parameter specified. The only currently supported types are authorization_code and refresh_token.

findings.text: Create a Stripe App using the CLI.
findings.quote: Create your Stripe App by running stripe apps create <app-name> in the CLI.

findings.text: Set the stripe_api_access_type to oauth in the app manifest.
findings.quote: Set stripe_api_access_type to oauth.

findings.text: Set the distribution_type to public in the app manifest.
findings.quote: Set distribution_type to public.

findings.text: Define allowed redirect URIs in the app manifest.
findings.quote: Set your allowed_redirect_uris. These are the URLs that users are redirected to after installing your app using OAuth.

findings.text: Upload the app to Stripe using the CLI.
findings.quote:
Upload your app to Stripe.

Command Line

stripe apps upload

findings.text: The authorization endpoint is at marketplace.stripe.com.
findings.quote: https://marketplace.stripe.com/oauth/v2/authorize?client_id=${clientId}&redirect_uri=${redirectUrl}&state=${state}.

findings.text: The token endpoint is at api.stripe.com.
findings.quote: curl -X POST https://api.stripe.com/v1/oauth/token

findings.text: The authorization code is valid for 5 minutes.
findings.quote: This authorisation code is single-use only and valid only for 5 minutes, in which your back end needs to exchange the code for the access token.

findings.text: Access tokens expire in 1 hour.
findings.quote: Access tokens expire in 1 hour, and refresh tokens expire after 1 year.

findings.text: Refresh tokens expire in 1 year.
findings.quote: Access tokens expire in 1 hour, and refresh tokens expire after 1 year.

findings.text: The supported grant type is authorization_code.
findings.quote: -d grant_type=authorization_code

findings.text: The supported grant type is refresh_token.
findings.quote: -d grant_type=refresh_token

findings.text: You must activate your Stripe account to publish an app.
findings.quote: You must activate your account.

findings.text: You can only publish one app per account.
findings.quote: You can only publish one app per account.

findings.text: The app review process takes 4 business days.
findings.quote: Submit your app for review (then wait 4 business days)

findings.text: The app manifest must not contain localhost or dummy URLs for redirect URIs.
findings.quote: The app manifest field allowed_redirect_uris must not contain localhost or dummy URLs. These entries pose a significant security risk and can enable unauthorised redirects.

findings.text: Set the distribution type to public in the app manifest.
findings.quote: stripe apps set distribution public

findings.text: Grant permissions for the app using the CLI.
findings.quote: stripe apps grant permission "PERMISSION_NAME" "EXPLANATION"

findings.text: Upload the app using the Stripe CLI.
findings.quote: stripe apps upload

findings.text: Stripe provides a specific URL format for OAuth authorization.
findings.quote: https://marketplace.stripe.com/oauth/v2/authorize?client_id=$(clientId)&redirect_uri=$(redirect_uri)&state=$(state)

findings.text: Stripe deprecated the Connect Stripe authentication method in favor of OAuth 2.0.
findings.quote: Stripe deprecated the Connect Stripe authentication method, so use this OAuth method instead.

findings.text: Test credentials provided for review must not require multi-factor authentication.
findings.quote: Disable multi-factor authentication or provide instructions for reviewers to pass it.

findings.text: Do not include custom cryptographic functions in your app code.
findings.quote: Your app code must comply with all applicable export control laws. Specifically, don’t include any custom cryptographic functions in your app. Custom cryptography is subject to the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR), and exporting such code outside the United States can result in severe penalties.

findings.text: Do not publish the same app under different names or categories.
findings.quote: Don’t publish the same app under different names or categories. Submit new versions of an app from the same account as the previous version.

findings.text: You must store secret materials for UI extensions using the Secret Store API.
findings.quote: You must properly store secret materials required by UI extensions using the Secret Store API

findings.text: The app manifest must specify if the app supports installation in a sandbox environment.
findings.quote: Your app manifest must specify whether your app supports installation in a sandbox environment. If set to false, your app won’t be available for installation in sandboxes.

findings.text: You can make your app publicly available on the Stripe App Marketplace.
findings.quote: The Stripe App Marketplace is how you share your application with the Stripe user community.

findings.text: You can share your app only with team members of your Stripe account.
findings.quote: For example, you might develop an app that sends sale data into your own custom accounting system. Or you might build an app that connects paid orders with your fulfilment system. For these and other situations, you can make the application only available to team members of your Stripe account.

findings.text: Apps published on the App Marketplace must go through a review process.
findings.quote: Stripe reviews all apps to make sure they comply with the published requirements before listing them in the marketplace.

findings.text: You cannot set a public distribution for another app if you already have a public app in the same account.
findings.quote: After you upload an app with a public distribution, you can’t set a public distribution for another app within the same Stripe account.

findings.text: Publicly distributed apps cannot contain specific restricted words in their names.
findings.quote: Beginning in September 2024, Stripe apps with a public distribution type can’t contain the words “Stripe”, “app”, “free” or “paid” in their names.

findings.text: Set the distribution type for your app using the Stripe CLI.
findings.quote: To set the distribution type for your app, run the following command: stripe apps set distribution public

findings.text: Submit the application for review to publish on the marketplace.
findings.quote: Submit the application for review.

findings.text: Read API requests must not exceed an average of 500 per transaction.
findings.quote: Your account’s read API requests must not exceed an average of 500 per transaction.

findings.text: Every account has a minimum allocation of 10,000 read requests per month.
findings.quote: Every account, regardless of transaction count, has a minimum allocation of 10,000 read requests per month.

findings.text: If you request a large limit increase, you must contact Stripe Support at least 6 weeks in advance.
findings.quote: If you request a large increase, contact Stripe Support at least 6 weeks in advance.

findings.text: Making changes after submitting an app for review will restart the review process.
findings.quote: If you make changes after submitting your app, we'll need to restart the review process.

findings.text: Apps must meet review guidelines to be available in the Stripe App Marketplace.
findings.quote: Once you’ve completed your submission, we’ll review your app to make sure it meets all of the review guidelines. If approved, you’ll be free to make your app available in the Stripe App Marketplace.

findings.text: To list an app on the Stripe App Marketplace, you must build the app and submit it for review.
findings.quote: App partners build an app and then submit it for app review to list it on the Stripe App Marketplace.

findings.text: To become a Stripe Partner, you must meet app requirements and pass the Stripe Apps review.
findings.quote: Meet app requirements and pass Stripe Apps review.
